claims.text: GDACS wildfire report for Serbia (event id 1030252, 05 Aug 2026 - 25 Aug 2026, latest EC/ECHO daily map update 24 Aug 2026): 'Forest fire can have a medium humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability'; burned area 18,310 hectares; 510 people in the burned area.

European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations, 'EU sends urgent support to Serbia as wildfires intensify' (24 August 2026): 'more than 3,500 hectares have already been impacted' at the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve; 'Serbia activated the civil protection mechanism on Friday 21 August'; the EU mobilised '4 helicopters from the strategic reserve of the rescEU fleet based in Czechia, Romania and Slovakia' plus 'ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania'; 'The fires have been ongoing for more than two weeks, fuelled by strong winds, challenging conditions, and terrain that is difficult to access'; the Copernicus emergency management service 'was already activated on 8 August'.

GDACS's wildfire report for Serbia (event id 1030252, episode 40, reporting window unchanged at 05 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC to 25 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area still 18,310 hectares and about 510 people in the burned area -- identical to the figures recorded in late August -- indicating no further fire growth has been detected in eleven days of subsequent automated episode updates.

description: Wildfires burned across Serbia from 5 August 2026, including the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve in Vojvodina, and on 21 August Serbia activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism for help. GDACS rated the event an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, with burned area holding at 18,310 hectares and about 510 people within the burned area since its 24 August update; GDACS's latest automated episode (5 September) shows no change in these figures, indicating the fire is now contained. The European Commission had reported more than 3,500 hectares impacted at Deliblato Sands, with the EU mobilising four rescEU helicopters from Czechia, Romania and Slovakia plus ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania; the Copernicus emergency mapping service was active from 8 August. No deaths or evacuation figures have been published by these sources.

impact.summary: GDACS records 18,310 hectares burned and about 510 people within the burned area over 5-25 August 2026, rated a medium humanitarian impact; the figure has remained unchanged through GDACS's episode 40 update (5 September 2026), eleven days after the last recorded fire growth, indicating the blaze is now contained. The European Commission reported more than 3,500 hectares impacted at the Deliblato Sands reserve, with four rescEU helicopters and German and Romanian ground teams deployed after Serbia's 21 August activation of the EU Civil Protection Mechanism. No deaths or evacuation figures have been published by these sources.
